_meta.indication: VERZENIO is indicated in combination with fulvestrant for the treatment of women with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer with disease progression following endocrine therapy; and as monotherapy for adult patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer with disease progression following endocrine therapy and prior chemotherapy in the metastatic setting.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial of abemaciclib plus fulvestrant vs placebo plus fulvestrant.
pivotal_trials.population: Women with HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer who had disease progression following endocrine therapy.
pivotal_trials.n: N=669 randomized (446 abemaciclib plus fulvestrant, 223 placebo plus fulvestrant).
pivotal_trials.result: Median PFS 16.4 months (abemaciclib+fulvestrant) vs 9.3 months (placebo+fulvestrant); HR 0.553 (95% CI 0.449, 0.681); p<.0001.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, single-arm, open-label trial of abemaciclib monotherapy.
pivotal_trials.population: Women with measurable HR-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer whose disease progressed during or after endocrine therapy, had received a taxane, and received 1 or 2 prior chemotherapy regimens in the metastatic setting.
pivotal_trials.n: 132 patients received at least one dose of treatment.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=20%) were diarrhea, neutropenia, nausea, abdominal pain, infections, fatigue, anemia, leukopenia, decreased appetite, vomiting, headache, and thrombocytopenia. In MONARCH 2, diarrhea occurred in 86% (vs 25% placebo), neutropenia 46% (vs 4%), and fatigue 46% (vs 32%). Serious risks include neutropenia (2 deaths from neutropenic sepsis), hepatotoxicity, and venous thromboembolism.
target_moa: Abemaciclib is a kinase inhibitor with activity against cyclin-dependent kinase 4 (CDK4) and CDK6; CDK4/6 in complex with D-type cyclins phosphorylate Rb protein, and inhibition leads to G1 cell cycle arrest in Rb-positive breast cancer cells.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held for this NDA; the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues unexpected for a drug of this class.

summary.text: Abemaciclib received Breakthrough Therapy Designation (Oct 2015) and Fast Track Designation (Nov 2015), and the NDA was granted Priority Review. It was approved during the first cycle without an advisory committee meeting or accelerated approval; approval was based on the Phase 3 MONARCH 2 PFS result and the single-arm Phase 2 MONARCH 1 ORR result.

citations.quote: **October 5, 2015:** FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation as metastatic breast cancer is a serious or life-threatening disease and preliminary clinical evidence generated by FIH Phase 1 Study JPBA appeared to demonstrate improvement in ORR in patients with HR-positive, HER2 negative metastatic breast cancer who had been treated with previous chemotherapies.
**November 12, 2015:** FDA granted Fast Track Designation for the investigation of abemaciclib for patients with refractory hormone receptor positive advanced or metastatic breast cancer.
No advisory committee meeting was held for this NDA.

requirement.text: Conduct Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling to evaluate the effect of repeat doses of a moderate CYP3A4 inducer on the PK of abemaciclib and its active metabolites and determine appropriate dosing recommendations; if inconclusive, conduct a PK trial.
